findings.claim: Legacy-layout complex obs (every complex obs on an upgraded install) get no I/O reduction at all: a read still costs 6 filesystem operations, 3 of them Files.exists, exactly as on master, so TRUNK-6682's first acceptance criterion ('at most one existence-related check') holds only for new-layout obs while the ticket would close as done.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is and TRUNK-6682 closes, upgraded local-storage installations, whose pre-2.8 obs all resolve through parseDataKey's legacy branch, keep paying master's 6 ops per read (exists(raw key) probes current + legacy = 2 Files.exists, then read() fails a stat on the current location and pays a 3rd Files.exists before stat+open), and nothing tracks the unmet half. The handler count tests only cover new-layout keys, so this cannot show up in CI. This is a reply in the open thread on AbstractHandlerTest (discussion 4070873940), which asked the same scope question before the read-first rewrite and has no answer; the new fact is that the rewrite fixed the new layout (6 to 3) and left legacy at 6 to 6. Under the constraint that parseDataKey keeps its exists() probe (ibacher's thread), 'at most one' is unreachable for legacy keys, so the resolution is probably to narrow the ticket or open a follow-up, which is the maintainers' call.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test (deleted) wrapping TextHandler.getObs(RAW_VIEW) and AbstractHandler.getObs in Mockito.mockStatic(Files.class, callRealMethod) counting exists/readAttributes/newInputStream, run on PR head and on a master worktree. New layout: master {exists=4, readAttributes=1, newInputStream=1}, PR {exists=1, readAttributes=1, newInputStream=1}. Legacy layout (<appdata>/obs/<name>, valueComplex 'title|<name>', data loaded = 5 bytes on both): master {exists=4, readAttributes=1, newInputStream=1}, PR {exists=3, readAttributes=2 (one throws NoSuchFileException), newInputStream=1}. Calibrated: the master new-layout 6 matches the earlier reviewer's independent instrumentation (4 exists + stat + open), and the PR new-layout 3 matches the PR description's own claim. Code path: AbstractHandler.parseDataKey:135 -> LocalStorageService.exists (two fileExists on a miss) -> LocalStorageService.read (failed reader.apply on current, fileExists(legacyPath), then stat + open).

findings.claim: TRUNK-6682 carries the backport label and describes a 2.8.x regression, but the new API is tagged '@since 3.0.0' only (StorageService.getDataWithMetadata, DataWithMetadata, the 3-arg injectMissingMetadata), and the change uses Java 16+ constructs (private record LoadedImage in ImageHandler, pattern-matching instanceof in S3StorageService.translateNotFound, @Deprecated(since=...)) that do not compile on the 2.8.x line, which built with javaCompilerVersion 1.8. Is this getting backported, and if so to which lines?
findings.evidence: Ticket snapshot: labels [backport, community-priority, performance], fixVersions []. StorageService.java:31 and ObjectMetadata.java:19 carry '@since 2.8.0, 2.7.5, 2.6.16, 2.5.15' (the storage API was backported before); the new members say only 3.0.0 (StorageService.java:197, DataWithMetadata.java:21, AbstractHandler.java ~168). `git show a085b50b6^:pom.xml` (last 2.8.0-SNAPSHOT pom before the 3.0.0 bump) has <javaCompilerVersion>1.8</javaCompilerVersion>. `javac --release 8` on a one-line file with a private record and `o instanceof String s` reports 'records are not supported in -source 8' and 'pattern matching in instanceof is not supported in -source 8'. Reply in the existing @since thread (discussion 4070873955), whose 'plus whatever maintenance lines it gets backported to' sub-point is still open.

verdict: Not ready to merge: the read-first rewrite does cut new-layout local reads from 6 to 3 filesystem ops and S3 reads to HEAD+GET, but legacy-layout obs still cost the same 6 ops as master, and whether TRUNK-6682 closes on this, which a reviewer asked before merge and nobody has answered, is still open.
what_i_swept: Step 1: confirmed diff stat (21 files, +967/-68; three-dot and two-dot stats identical, so no drift); read the PR body, ticket snapshot and all 31 inline comments, 11 reviews and 13 PR comments; checked each prior thread against the head (default method on StorageService, DataWithMetadata now a formatted class, shared internal helpers in LocalStorageService plus the metadata-before-data comment, NoSuchFileException documented, URI_VIEW metadata restored with a test, ImageHandler legacy filename fallback restored and the unrelated obs-dir guard dropped, S3 multipart length via Content-Range with a mocked-client test, FileSystemException fallback for over-long legacy names with the obs dir created in the test, exists() containment kept, S3 getData delegating, the 2-arg injectMissingMetadata deprecated, AbstractHandler count test restored, a legacy test for getDataWithMetadata added). All resolved except the ticket-scope thread (F1) and the backport sub-point of the @since thread (F2). Step 2: solution fit checked against the ticket's three acceptance criteria by measurement on PR and master for new and legacy layouts; the approach (read-first with a legacy fallback inside LocalStorageService, one combined read via a default interface method) compared with caching the layout resolution and with dropping parseDataKey's probe, the latter ruled out by ibacher's thread. Step 3: read every changed main file in full; traced outward to every caller of getData/getMetadata/exists/injectMissingMetadata (git grep) and every StorageService implementation in the tree (Local, S3, test doubles); compared each handler's missing-file and IOException paths with master (BinaryStream/BinaryData/Text: missing file still ends in IllegalArgumentException from Assert.notNull, other IOException now APIException; AbstractHandler/URI_VIEW still UncheckedIOException); checked path-containment behaviour of read()/exists() against master's legacy-first getPath; checked S3 404 translation down the ExecutionException cause chain; checked the backport target's Java level from pom history. Mutation controls: making LocalStorageService.getDataWithMetadata skip the legacy fallback turns LocalStorageServiceTest.getDataWithMetadata_shouldReturnDataAndMetadataWhenLegacyFileExists red (NoSuchFileException), and making MediaHandler pass null metadata turns MediaHandlerTest.getObs_shouldReadDataAndMetadataInASingleStorageCall red (getMetadataCalls 1, expected 0); both files restored. Pass 1 surfaced F1, pass 2 (backport, consumers, implementations, mutation controls) surfaced F2, and pass 3 (exception paths, S3 translation, containment, test realism) found nothing new of substance. S3: ran S3StorageServiceIT against the local adobe/s3mock:4.5.0 container (29 tests, 0 skipped, all green), including the inherited getDataWithMetadata tests and a temporary test that getMetadata and getData on a missing key throw NoSuchFileException. Control: making translateNotFound return the raw IOException turned exactly those two tests red (IOException instead of NoSuchFileException). Test and source restored.
could_not_verify: Whether the change compiles on a 2.8.x maintenance branch needs access: that branch's sources are not in this clone and reading the repository on GitHub is out of bounds, so F2 rests on the 2.8.0-SNAPSHOT pom's javaCompilerVersion 1.8 plus a javac --release 8 check of the constructs, and stays a question.
Whether TRUNK-6682 should cover legacy-layout reads or be narrowed needs your decision (the maintainers'), so F1's resolution may be a ticket edit rather than code.
